# ARC line-and-object transformation

Use this when task examples show a uniform background, a full grid-spanning line in one color, and a separate object of another color.

## Rule observed
- The full line remains unchanged.
- The object shifts by one cell toward the full-length line.
- The vacated cells from its original footprint are filled with color 8, forming a full line parallel to the divider, immediately on the far side of the object's original location.
- The object shape/color is preserved in its shifted location. Background and other cells remain unchanged.

## Demonstrated cases
- Horizontal divider row 3, object below it: object moves up one row and a full row of 8 appears immediately below the old object's lower edge (the example's added row was row 6; object had occupied rows 4–5). This corresponds to the vacated row as object shifts toward the divider.
- Vertical divider column 0, object to its right: object shifts left one column; full column of 8 fills vacated far-right edge of object's bounding box. Example object at column 3 shifted to column 1, new column 2 is 8. For irregular shape, translate all its colored cells by one column toward divider; the 8-line is at the old object's far boundary column.

## Practical steps
1. Identify background, divider color, object color, divider orientation and side containing object.
2. Translate the object exactly one cell toward the divider (do not alter its shape).
3. Draw a complete parallel line in color 8 at the far side of the original object, replacing the object cells that are vacated according to the demonstrated rule.
4. Leave divider/background otherwise intact and verify dimensions/cell locations.
